archetype.name: Pocket Passer (veteran rhythm)
archetype.definition: A 38-year-old timing thrower who wins from the pocket by getting the ball out before pressure lands and hitting throws past the sticks, with essentially no running game and a long history of giving the ball away.

report.headline: Veteran rhythm passer whose value lives downfield, but turnovers are swallowing the gains lately
report.take:
Cousins at 38 is what he has been for a decade: a pocket passer who reads it, sets, and throws on time. He offers nothing as a runner. That's 0.69 yards a carry, and his seven scrambles produced zero first downs. But he almost never takes the sack that kills a drive: a 3.8% sack rate (6th of 55) and a pressure-to-sack rate of 17.1% (4th of 45). The bigger story is that he looks sharper than he did a year ago in Atlanta. CPOE is up 4.4 points, yards per attempt up 0.84, and the bad-throw rate down 2.1. On a season line he sits 11th in passing yards per game and 13th in EPA per game, with a pace of 4,299 yards and 34 touchdowns.

All of his value comes from one place: throws of 10 or more air yards. Those 134 attempts added 51.6 EPA, more than his whole dropback total. Everything under 10 yards netted out to roughly zero (-0.002 a play), and the screens and swings behind the line cost 17.3 points. The deep ball has been excellent: 0.687 EPA a throw, with a CPOE of 6.8 on 38 attempts. Third down is the other pillar, at 0.373 EPA a play, 11 touchdowns against one interception, and a 48.7% conversion rate. He keeps drives alive by throwing past the sticks rather than to them. His tight end is the main beneficiary, at 0.459 EPA a target on 70 looks.

What the season line hides is the cost of that aggressiveness. His aggressive-throw rate (19.5%) is above almost every season of his career, and the interceptions have followed. Ten picks rank 51st of 55, and five came in intermediate throws, where his CPOE goes negative. The middle of the field is the problem zone: a -9.3 CPOE with four picks on 97 throws. None of this is new. He finished near the bottom of the league in interceptions in 2020, 2022 and 2024. Over the last three games it has boiled over: five interceptions, a 5% pick rate, and EPA per dropback down to 0.013 from 0.129 for the season. Two of those three games came against San Francisco's 10th-ranked defense. Tellingly, his accuracy hasn't slipped; CPOE is actually up 1.8 in that span. This is a decision-and-explosiveness slump, not a mechanical one.

The red zone also flatters him a bit. Sixteen touchdowns came on a 32.4% success rate and 46.9% completions inside the 20, so the scoring rate is likely to cool. He is also bad at protecting leads: down to -0.211 EPA a play with three picks when ahead by nine or more. The usage picture is murky too. The team's start log credits Kyler Murray with most of the season's starts, and Murray's hamstring return date is this week. Cousins is the listed QB1 for now, so the outlook depends as much on that as on his play. When he plays, expect around 230-250 yards and a couple of scores in good matchups, with an interception always in play.

strengths.title: Value lives past ten yards
strengths.body: All of his net passing value comes from throws of 10 or more air yards, and his deep ball is among the most efficient throws he makes. It comes from anticipation and willingness to push the ball rather than arm talent. The skill has held across his career, but the deep sample is only 38 attempts, so the exact rate will drift down.

strengths.title: Third-down conversion engine
strengths.body: On third down he facing an average of 7.3 yards to go, and he throws past the sticks rather than checking down, which is why the EPA is so high. Eleven touchdowns against one interception on 107 attempts is unusually clean for him. Some of that will cool, but the habit of attacking past the marker is stable.

strengths.title: Avoids sacks by timing
strengths.body: He doesn't escape pressure; he beats it with a 2.86-second release and a willingness to throw on rhythm. That keeps the sack rate near the top of the league even with a mid-pack pressure rate. This trait is consistent across his career and should hold.

concerns.title: Interceptions are the price tag
concerns.body: His aggressiveness is up, and the turnovers came with it: 10 picks, near the bottom of the league, with a recent spike to a 5% interception rate. Most of the damage comes on intermediate and middle-of-field throws, where his accuracy falls off. Given his career, this is a real trait, not bad luck, though the recent rate should ease toward his season norm.

concerns.title: Recent efficiency collapse
concerns.body: Over the last three games his EPA per dropback has nearly vanished and his adjusted net yards per dropback fell sharply. Accuracy actually improved over that stretch, so the drop comes from turnovers and fewer explosive plays against good defenses. Expect a partial bounce rather than a return to his early-season peak.

concerns.title: Red zone and lead protection
concerns.body: His touchdown total outruns his red-zone efficiency: a low success rate and sub-50% completions there. He is also poor with a two-score lead, where he has thrown three interceptions. The red-zone touchdown rate is the likeliest stat on his line to regress. The lead split is a small sample but fits his turnover profile.

trend.note: He was steady and efficient through mid-season, peaking with a 14.0-EPA game against the Jets in Week 8. Since then, two San Francisco games and a Week 9 three-interception day dragged his last three games to near-zero EPA, though the Green Bay win showed his clean, quick-game version.

nextGame.headline: Soft pass defense and his former team, but script may cap volume
nextGame.body:
Atlanta, his former club, sits in the bottom half of the league against quarterbacks. It ranks 27th in fantasy points allowed to the position and 26th in touchdowns allowed per game, with a mid-pack pass defense by EPA. It doesn't sack the quarterback much, which lets his rhythm game work, though it does land hits. It also isn't a defense that gives up the deep shots he lives on, ranking 9th on deep EPA. The bigger pull is game script. Minnesota is a 7-point home favorite behind the league's top defense, facing a bottom-tier, run-leaning Atlanta passing offense. If the Vikings build a lead, Cousins' volume and efficiency both tend to drop.

Availability cuts both ways. Jordan Addison, a 92%-snap receiver, is out after thumb surgery, which thins the outside options. That should push even more volume to the tight end and backs, who already carry much of his target share. On Atlanta's side, linebacker Divine Deablo (78% of snaps) is out. That could open the middle of the field, his weakest zone this season. Kyler Murray remains listed out with a hamstring strain, and Cousins is QB1. The game is indoors.

keyMatchups.title: Middle of field without Deablo
keyMatchups.body: Cousins has been least accurate and most turnover-prone between the numbers. Losing a starting linebacker weakens Atlanta's middle coverage. That is the throw window where his tight end does damage and where his interceptions usually come from.

keyMatchups.title: Light pass rush, clean pocket
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta's sack rate ranks in the bottom third, and Cousins already avoids sacks as well as almost anyone. A clean pocket gives him time to set his feet on the intermediate throws, where his accuracy has slipped.

keyMatchups.title: Lead script and run-heavy opponent
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta passes far less than expected and its passing offense ranks near the bottom, so possessions may be short and slow. As a big favorite, Minnesota could spend the second half protecting a lead, which is his worst game state.

nextGame.watch: Whether his intermediate throws over the middle come out clean. If the interceptions stop there, the soft matchup turns into a multi-touchdown day.

restOfSeason.body:
The core of his game should hold: a quick release that avoids sacks, efficient throws past the sticks, and accuracy that is genuinely better than last season. The recent slump looks driven by turnovers and tough opponents, not decline, so expect his efficiency to recover toward the middle of the league rather than stay near zero. Two things should cool. His red-zone touchdown rate is out of line with how often he actually succeeds inside the 20, and a deep ball this hot on 38 attempts will come down. A reasonable range is 225-260 yards and 1.3-1.9 touchdowns a game, with about one interception per start.

The larger unknown is the job itself. Murray's hamstring return date is this week, and the start log shows Murray as the season's primary starter. If Murray comes back healthy, Cousins could go back to the bench. Addison's return would help him by giving the passing game another outside option.
swingFactors: Kyler Murray's hamstring return and who starts
Jordan Addison's return from thumb surgery
Whether the intermediate interceptions settle back down

confidence.note: His passing profile is steady across his career, but the QB start log conflicts with his game log and Murray's return date makes his role uncertain.
